accepted.question_text: For the self-adjoint differential operator LTW,s acting on L^2([s,+infinity)) and defined by LTW,s := d/dx alpha_s d/dx + beta_s with alpha_s(x) = x - s and beta_s(x) = -x(x - s), study its eigenvectors.
accepted.context_brief: Eigenvectors for the Tracy-Widom commuting operator

evidence.quote: To sumarise : Question 1. Study the eigenvectors of the operator LTW,s := d/dx alpha_s d/dx + beta_s, alpha_s(x) := x - s, beta_s(x) := -x(x - s).

accepted.question_text: Let Kn be the restriction to L^2([s,+infinity)) of the projection onto the first n probabilistic Hermite functions, with kernel Kn(x, y) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} phi_k(x) phi_k(y). Can one find a differential operator commuting with Kn on L^2([s,+infinity)), and what are its eigenvectors? The operator need not be second order, but it should converge in a suitable rescaled sense to LTW,s.
accepted.context_brief: Commuting operator for the finite-n GUE kernel

evidence.quote: The GUE kernel operator is the restriction to L^2([s, +infinity)) of the projection on the first n vectors of L^2(R) with the (probabilistic) Hermite functions, i.e. Kn(x, y) := sum_{k=0}^{n-1} phi_k(x) phi_k(y).

Question 2. Can one find a commuting differential operator to Kn acting on L^2([s, +infinity)) ? What are its eigenvectors ? Such an operator is not necessarily of the second order, but it should converge in some sense to LTW,s when suitably rescaled.

accepted.question_text: Given a finite numerical sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^n, define the polynomial P_n(z) by P_n(z) = sum_{k=0}^n f_k f_{n-k} binom(n,k) [(z)_k (z)_{n-k} - (z+1)_k (z-1)_{n-k}], where (z)_k is the Pochhammer symbol. If the generating polynomial sum_{k=0}^n f_k z^k has only real negative zeros, must the polynomial P_n(z) also have only real negative zeros?

evidence.quote: For a given finite numerical sequence {fk}_k=0^n define the polynomial Pn(z) by Pn(z)=sum_{k=0}^n fk f_{n-k} binom(n,k) [(z)_k (z)_{n-k} - (z + 1)_k (z - 1)_{n-k}], where (z)_0 = 1, (z)_k = z(z + 1) ... (z + k - 1), k >= 1, is the Pochhammer symbol.
Conjecture 1. Suppose the polynomial sum_{k=0}^n fk z^k has only real negative zeros. Then the same is true for the polynomial Pn(z) defined above.

accepted.question_text: For the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomials P_n^r(z) built from a finite sequence {f_k}_{k=0}^n, if the polynomial sum_{k=0}^n f_k z^k has only real negative zeros, must P_n^r(z) also have only real negative zeros for every r >= 2?

evidence.quote: A similar conjecture can be also be stated for polynomials formed by higher order Toeplitz determinants, namely, P_n^r(z) := ... It is probably not too hard to prove that the polynomial P_n^r(z) has degree n - r(r - 1).
Conjecture 2. Suppose the polynomial sum_{k=0}^n fk z^k has only real negative zeros. Then the same holds for the polynomial P_n^r(z) for each r >= 2.

accepted.question_text: Suppose {f_k}_{k=0}^n is a finite Polya frequency sequence of order d >= r. Must the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomial P_n^r(z) be Hurwitz stable, meaning that all of its zeros lie in the open left half-plane?
accepted.context_brief: Hurwitz stability of higher-order Toeplitz determinants

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3. Suppose {fk}_k=0^n is a finite Polya frequency sequence of order d >= r. Then the polynomial P_n^r(z) is Hurwitz stable (all its zeros lie on the open left half-plane). In particular, it has positive coefficients.

accepted.question_text: Let positive real parameters a1, ..., ad, b and positive integers m1, ..., md be such that the hypergeometric generating function satisfies _{d+1}F_d(a1+m1, ..., ad+md, b ; a1, ..., ad ; x) = A(x) / (1 - x)^(m+b), where m = sum_j m_j and A(x) is a polynomial. Find sufficient conditions on a1, ..., ad, b, m1, ..., md that guarantee that A(x) has only real zeros, equivalently only negative zeros.

evidence.quote: Suppose a1, a2, ..., ad, b > 0 are real and m1, m2, ..., md > 0 are integer. Define the polynomial A(x) by _{d+1}F_d(a1 + m1, a2 + m2, ..., ad + md, b ; a1, a2, ..., ad ; x) = A(x) / (1 - x)^(m+b).
Open problem. Find sufficient conditions on a1, a2, ..., ad, b, m1, m2, ..., md ensuring that A(x) has only real zeros (only negative zeros).

accepted.question_text: Let V be an external field on C, meaning a continuous function V : C -> R union {+infinity}, not identically +infinity, such that lim_{|z| -> infinity} (V(z) - log(1 + |z|)) = +infinity. For each n, let P_n be the unique monic polynomial of degree n satisfying the orthogonality relations integral_C P_n(z) z^k e^{-n V(z)} dA(z) = 0 for k = 0, 1, ..., n - 1, and let nu(P_n) be its normalized zero counting measure. Find external fields V for which nu(P_n) converges weakly to a limit measure mu_V as n -> infinity, and characterize the limiting measure mu_V.
accepted.context_brief: Zero-counting limits for complex orthogonal polynomials

evidence.quote: Let P be a monic polynomial of degree n with zeros z1, ..., zn, listed according multiplicities. We use nu(P) = 1/n sum_j delta_{z_j} to denote the normalized zero counting measure of P.

An external field on C is a continuous function V : C -> R union {+infinity}, not identically +infinity, with lim_{|z|->infinity} (V(z) - log(1 + |z|)) = +infinity. The growth condition guarantees that, for each n, there is a unique monic polynomial Pn of degree n such that integral_C Pn(z) z^k e^{-nV(z)} dA(z) = 0, k = 0, 1, ..., n - 1.

Problem. Find external fields V such that the sequence of normalized zero counting measures of the orthogonal polynomials (2) has a weak limit, say nu(Pn) -> mu_V as n -> infinity, and characterize the limiting measure mu_V.

accepted.question_text: Let mu be a nonnegative continuous majorant on [-1,1], and let omega_mu in P_n be the associated snake polynomial, meaning the unique degree-n polynomial that oscillates most between plus and minus mu at an alternation set. Find a class of majorants mu for which the associated snake polynomials Q_n have a Chebyshev expansion Q_n = sum_{i=0}^n a_i T_i whose coefficients are either all nonnegative or strictly sign-alternating, in the sense that a_i a_{i+1} < 0 for every i.

evidence.quote: Consider a majorant mu in C[-1, 1], mu(x) >= 0, x in [-1, 1]. If there exists P in Pn, P != 0, such that -mu(x) <= P(x) <= mu(x), x in [-1, 1], then there exists a unique polynomial omega_mu in Pn called snake polynomial associated with mu, which oscillates most between plus and minus mu.

Open problem. Find a class of majorants mu for which the associated snake polynomials Qn have non-negative or sign alternating expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind, i.e. Qn = sum_{i=0}^n a_i T_i with all a_i >= 0 or with a_i a_{i+1} < 0 for all i.

accepted.question_text: If mu is a nonnegative continuous even convex function on [-1,1], must the snake polynomials associated with mu have a nonnegative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind?
accepted.context_brief: Chebyshev positivity for even convex majorants

evidence.quote: Conjecture (G.N.) If mu >= 0 is a continuous even convex function in [-1, 1], then the associated with mu snake polynomials have non-negative expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind.

accepted.question_text: Fix d - 2 < s < d and consider the annulus B_{r,R} = {x in R^d : r <= |x| <= R}. Find the equilibrium measure mu* supported on B_{r,R} that minimizes the Riesz s-energy I_s(mu) = integral integral K_s(x - y) dmu(x) dmu(y) among all probability measures supported on that annulus.
accepted.context_brief: Riesz equilibrium measure on an annulus

evidence.quote: For -2 < s < d, the Riesz energy of a probability measure mu on R^d is Is(mu) := integral integral Ks(x - y) dmu(x) dmu(y).

Equilibrium open problem for multi-dimensional annulus. Given d - 2 < s < d, find an equilibrium measure on an annulus B_{r,R} := {x in R^d : r <= |x| <= R}, i.e. the measure mu* such that mu* = arg min_{supp(mu) subset B_{r,R}} Is(mu).

accepted.question_text: Let P be a univariate polynomial of degree d >= 2, and for integers n >= 1 and 0 <= m <= nd define Q_{n,m}(x) = d^m(P(x)^n)/dx^m. Let Upsilon_P be the closure of the union of all roots of all Q_{n,m}(x). If the roots of P are in convex position but do not form a regular polygon, must Upsilon_P be a closed domain inside the convex hull of the roots of P, with all critical points of P on the boundary of Upsilon_P, no inflection points on that boundary, and boundary contained in the union of the critical values, with respect to z, of F_alpha(z) = z - alpha P(z)/P'(z) as alpha ranges over [0,d]?

evidence.quote: Consider the double-indexed polynomial family Qn,m(x) = d^m P^n(x) / dx^m, where 0 <= m <= nd. Obviously, for any pair of non-negative integers (n, m), all roots of Qn,m(x) lie in the convex hull of the roots of P(x). Consider the union of all roots of all Qn,m(x) with 0 <= m <= nd and denote the closure of the latter countable set as Upsilon_P - the shadow of the polynomial P(z).

Conjecture 1. For any polynomial P of degree at least 3 whose roots are in convex position, but do not form a regular polygon, (i) Upsilon_P is a closed domain in the convex hull of the roots of P. (ii) All critical points of P lie on the boundary of Upsilon_P. (iii) the boundary of Upsilon_P has no inflection points. (iv) The boundary of Upsilon_P is contained in the union of all critical values (w.r.t. z) of the rational function F_alpha(z) = z - alpha P(z)/P'(z), where the parameter alpha runs over the interval [0, d].

accepted.question_text: For any configuration of N fixed electric charges in R^3 that has only finitely many equilibrium points, is the number of equilibrium points always at most (N - 1)^2?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 (J. C. Maxwell). For any configuration of N fixed electric charges in R^3 having finitely many points of equilibrium, the number of the latter points is at most (N - 1)^2.

accepted.question_text: Does every configuration of N positive electric charges in R^d have only finitely many equilibrium points?
accepted.context_brief: Finiteness of equilibria for positive charges

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3. Any configuration of N positive electric charges in R^d has only finitely many points of equilibrium.
